beats.en_subtitle: Here is the master summary connecting all eight key principles of futures mechanics.

ui_state.heading: Today's thread
steps: Futures contracts are standardized exchange agreements where a Long agrees to buy and a Short agrees to sell an asset at a future date
Over 99% of futures positions are closed out before delivery by executing the exact opposite trade in the same contract month
In Business Snapshot 2.1, buying instead of selling to close left a trader with 2 contracts and 80,000 lbs of cattle 2,000 miles away
Total futures gain or loss equals Contract Size multiplied by the difference between entry and exit futures prices
Exchanges specify asset grades and adjustments like CME Corn No. 1 (+1.5 cents) and No. 3 (-1.5 cents) or US Grade A Orange Juice (62.5 Brix)
Contract sizes and quotes vary from $100,000 Treasury Bonds quoted in 1/32nds to Mini Nasdaq 100 contracts set at 20 times the index
Daily price limits (Limit Up and Limit Down) curb single-day volatility while Position Limits prevent speculators from cornering a market
As delivery arrives, arbitrage forces the futures price to converge to the spot price (F_T = S_T) because any gap creates riskless profit
ui_state.bottomTakeaway: Less than 1% of futures contracts result in physical delivery, yet the legal threat of delivery is the invisible anchor that ties futures prices to real-world spot prices.
